definition: The flexion reflex is a pain-related withdrawal response in which flexor muscles are activated. In this packet, the nociceptive flexion reflex is used as a behavioral measure of mechanical pain sensitivity or threshold.

reasons: The packet text does not explicitly define the flexion reflex as “a pain-related withdrawal response in which flexor muscles are activated,” nor does it describe flexor muscle activation as part of the reflex.

While the packet does state that “The nociceptive flexion reflex was tested using an analgesy-meter” and that “intrathecal administration of ML297 increased the mechanical nociceptive threshold,” it does not clearly support the specific wording that it is “a pain-related withdrawal response” with “flexor muscles” activated.

The packet supports that the nociceptive flexion reflex was used to assess mechanical nociceptive threshold, but it does not define the flexion reflex as a pain-related withdrawal response with activation of flexor muscles.
The field is not supported by the packet, which treats the reflex as a nociceptive/pain measure rather than a learning concept.
